item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: FilesService.Upload uses the established multipart helper and delegates to FilesService.Add, with an end-to-end retry test using a non-seekable reader. A duplicates Add’s request/response machinery in direct conflict with the required routing.","reasons":["B calls multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content) and then s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.","B directly tests the reported behavior: a streamed, non-seekable input survives a 429 and is successfully resent when RetryAllMethods is enabled.","A bypasses FilesService.Add and reimplements its internals, including option processing, headers, Raw.Do, response decoding, and missing-data handling; this violates an explicit contract requirement and creates maintenance drift.","A’s added retry test only establishes generic bytes.Reader replayability, not that FilesService.Upload produces and submits a replayable multipart body after a 429."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add instead of routing through it, so future fixes or semantic changes to Add may not apply to Upload.","The Upload test checks the field and filename but does not verify uploaded content, retry behavior, validation, or source-reader errors.","Its generic retry test does not exercise multipart encoding or FilesService.Upload."],"risks_b":["It unnecessarily adds PersonsService.UploadPicture and its test, expanding the public API outside the requested scope and conflicting with the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.","The basic multipart test does not read and assert the uploaded file content.","Visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures as explicitly requested."]}
